name: The Long Morning
summary: There is a further shore, and the way to it is open to anybody, and almost nobody goes.
body: Nangijala is not the last place. This is not in dispute, which is unusual for anything in this book.

Every so often somebody here stops being here. Not the Quiet — nothing like the Quiet. A person who is entirely Bright, entirely themselves, who has got all the way back to their own name and their own face and the road home and does not need one other living soul to hold any of it for them, will one evening simply not be in the room, and everybody who knew them will find that they remember them perfectly and feel no grief at all, which is the strangest part of the whole business.
And that night the northern sky lights up.

The tellers call it the Long Morning, and they call the lights the far edge of somebody else's dawn, seen from underneath. It is a beautiful thing to say and there is no evidence for it whatsoever. Nobody has come back. Not once, not ever, not a word.
The Chroniclers regard that silence as disqualifying and have said so at length. The fire-keepers regard it as the entire point, and have said so at greater length.

What is not in dispute is that the way is open, and that it is open to everybody, and that it appears to cost nothing at all. Remember yourself completely and you may go on. That is the requirement, and it is the only requirement, and it has never once been observed to fail.

So the question a new star always eventually asks — usually about a year in, usually at somebody's fire, usually with the face of a person who thinks they have spotted something everybody else has missed — is why on earth is anybody still here.
The answers are not complicated. Almost nobody's is.

There are people waiting for somebody who has not fallen yet, and who will not go on ahead of them, and who have been standing at the meeting-places for a very long time getting slowly stranger. There are people who did fall, and whose person fell too, and thinned, and is still out there as a shape doing something faithful and empty; and they will not leave a thing that still has their name in its mouth. There are people who did something in the life before this one and cannot make going on feel like anything but getting away with it.
And there are the keepers, who could go tomorrow, and who have the rota.

Ask anybody here why they are still here and they will tell you, if you have sat with them long enough. Everybody in Nangijala has an answer to that question. It is the answer that makes them a person rather than a shape.
